BiblicalUsage: Ziyv is the Aramaic word for brightness or splendour, and Daniel uses it for what can be seen on a face and on an image. The great image of Nebuchadnezzar's dream had a terrible brightness, and the king's own face lost its brightness when the writing appeared on the wall. Daniel's own countenance changed too, when the visions troubled him.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe brightness in Daniel is a window into the heart — what shines on the outside tells what is happening inside.
